answer.worked:
Factor the quadratic denominator and combine the fractions in the divisor.
$$\begin{align*}\dfrac{\dfrac{3}{x^2-x-6}}{\dfrac{2}{x+2}+\dfrac{1}{x-3}}&=\dfrac{3}{(x-3)(x+2)}\div\dfrac{2(x-3)+(x+2)}{(x+2)(x-3)}\\\dfrac{\dfrac{3}{x^2-x-6}}{\dfrac{2}{x+2}+\dfrac{1}{x-3}}&=\dfrac{3}{(x-3)(x+2)}\times\dfrac{(x+2)(x-3)}{3x-4}\\\dfrac{\dfrac{3}{x^2-x-6}}{\dfrac{2}{x+2}+\dfrac{1}{x-3}}&=\dfrac{3}{3x-4}.\end{align*}$$
The original denominators require $x\ne-2,3$. The divisor must also be nonzero, so $x\ne\dfrac43$.
